utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The record and this evidence is speaking for itself, so I think maybe it's a matter for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The armed conflict is agreed among the parties, so there is no need to go into all those details. Can you move on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour. I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Popovic, what's your personal knowledge or information? Where were you at the beginning of the outbreak of armed conflict, and where were you in the night between the 16th and 17th of April, 1992? Please try to explain this to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC
utterances.text: This is being insisted upon, the point whether this is my personal observation or not. However, I did have occasion. I refer to Mr. Milos Bogdanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no. Please, please, Mr. Popovic. This has been sufficiently clarified. The Trial Chamber passed a decision on this. Our time is limited. Please answer my question. My question was fairly simple: Where were you during the night between the 16th and 17th of April, 1992? And please describe what you heard then, what you saw. Please, tell us about that particular period of time, on the basis of your direct personal experience.

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC
utterances.text: I was in Crkvina at that time. There was a group of people in Crkvina, different people, people with different backgrounds, who had come, and I said then that Samac was to be taken on that night. And people went to a gathering in the centre of the village, and I came too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Slow down, please, Mr. Popovic. When you say "a group of people," what people were those?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC
utterances.text: At first, most of the people who were there were the locals from Crkvina. They came to the centre of the village. And then people from other local communes began to arrive, and the roads leading to the town were in a way closed. And then the shooting began in the town. I couldn't know immediately who attacked whom. It was only in the early-morning hours that we found out there had been fighting between members of certain forces in the town itself, the forces that were stationed in the town, the SDA and the HDZ, as well as members of the Serbian side. After that, during the next day, I went to the town, to the outskirts, to the Pik factory in Samac, where I found a great number of people who were angry [as interpreted], and they were saying: What's going on? And, Who attacked whom? There was constant firing, constant fire, and there was fighting in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that, Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I heard the witness saying that "people were curious," not "angry." Here on page 90, line 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Correction. Mr. Popovic, can you hear me now? Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We did have some technical problems. Mr. Popovic, who did you mean when you said that in Crkvina you gathered with the locals, after the outbreak of conflict in the night between the 16th and 17th of April? Who exactly did you have in mind when you said that Samac was to be taken, or taken over? Which side were you referring to when you said that? What exactly did you talk about with the locals?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the information that I had and that other people had, the other side was supposed to take over Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What is the name of the other side? Please, Mr. Popovic: I just warn you again. Try to speak slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, once again, number one, some of this -- I don't know if it's a translation problem or just incoherent: "And it's in view of the information I had and other people had." Once again, what information are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I will clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And he's saying he heard some things. What has he seen? Once again, he's a fact witness. Let's hear some facts, not just -- he's talking rumours and it's not clear who is saying what, what people are here. I don't know if we're talking about the Serbian paramilitaries of this group from -- that's arrived. I don't know who he's talking about. It's not clear from the transcript, or at least the last page or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure Mr. Pantelic can clarify that so that we can follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. That is just my intention to clarify that with the witness, exactly the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Popovic, you said that in Crkvina, because you had heard that there was fighting and shooting, you had gathered together with the locals in Crkvina. There were many people there, and you spoke about the taking of Samac, or the taking over of Samac. I'm asking you now: Based on your information, based on your personal knowledge, which was the side that was to take Samac? Please avoid such categories and concepts as "this side," "that side," "we" or "they." Please use the following categories: Serbs, Croats, Muslims, or specific institutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd object to that. That's strict speculation, how much this witness can show that he's a member of some military organisation, had plans, intercepted plans.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Well, perhaps he could have heard from some people.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please tell us: The night between the 16th and the 17th, Crkvina, it's locals gathered. What did you talk about specifically? What did you hear there?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC
utterances.text: I think that was no rumour. If someone who is in charge of the mobilisation and someone who is the head of an organisation --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. Stop, please, Mr. Popovic. You've already explained that.

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: We're talking about the night between the 16th and the 17th in Crkvina. You mentioned that the locals were talking about Samac and that Samac was to be taken, and so on and so forth. My specific question is: Samac was supposed to be taken by whom exactly? What was the whole thing about?

utterances.speaker: SAVO POPOVIC
utterances.text: Samac was supposed to be taken by the SDA and the HDZ. The Serbian side came into conflict with the HDZ and the SDA, who had armed units of their own, and fighting broke out between the Serbian side and the other side, which included Croats and Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Popovic. Thank you for all your explanations. We'll speak again tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We shall adjourn now and continue our proceedings tomorrow at 0900 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: 1.45 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 6th day of February 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
